source_user: Advanced cluster case RDMA-95: Explain how RDMA changes the data path for multi-node GPU training or inference. Variant 95 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: separate verbs, queues, memory registration, transport selection, bandwidth, latency, and fallback behavior; compare measured device counters with application-level communication time. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume a multi-node GPU job on an RDMA-capable fabric; verify NIC, switch, transport, collective library, GPU/NIC PCIe placement, topology, and software versions instead of inferring them. The data path is: the application or collective library posts verbs work requests to send/receive or RDMA read/write queue pairs; buffers must satisfy the relevant registration and access rules; the NIC transfers payloads over the selected transport and completions, synchronization, errors, or a fallback path determine what the application sees. This mechanism does not guarantee a speedup: host copies, CPU polling, registration, queue depth, message size, congestion, topology, PCIe placement, and synchronization may dominate.

Hypothesis: with model, global batch, message-size distribution, node count, topology, software, clocks, and background load held fixed, the intended RDMA path lowers median and p99 collective communication time (ms) and CPU time per step, and increases effective throughput (samples/s or tokens/s), without increasing error or timeout rates. Measure application timestamps for all-reduce/all-gather or inference transfers, payload bytes, achieved bandwidth (GB/s), p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), overlap, queue-pair depth/completions, NIC bytes/errors/retransmits, GPU utilization, host CPU, PCIe counters, and end-to-end step latency. Compare against a verified non-RDMA or known-good baseline using matched workloads, warm-up removal, repeated randomized trials, confidence intervals, and synchronized clocks; report topology, units, sample counts, and raw-trace provenance. Device counters alone cannot establish application benefit.

For a link or path failure, first stop claiming RDMA benefit, capture error/completion, link, route, congestion, and collective logs, and bound retries/timeouts. Drain or quarantine the affected path and use a tested alternate transport only if correctness and capacity are preserved; otherwise pause the job. Roll back the configuration if p99 latency, timeout/error rate, correctness, or throughput breaches the predeclared gate, then restore the last known-good settings and canary before re-enabling. Evidence required: fabric/NIC configuration and topology, workload and baseline traces, controlled A/B analysis, failure-injection results, and confirmation that no fallback masked the fault. Do not expose unverified credentials or claim platform-specific facts.

fallback traffic can mask the primary fault
tail-latency evidence is confounded by topology and workload
evidence_required: verified topology and configuration
matched baseline and repeated A/B traces
application and device counters with units
fault-injection and rollback/canary results

source_user: Advanced cluster case RoCE-1: Diagnose a RoCE-based GPU cluster whose collective communication has unstable tail latency. Variant 1 must state assumptions, define a falsifiable hypothesis, name metrics, and include one failure or rollback condition.
source_assistant: An expert answer should distinguish model-domain mechanisms from runtime measurements. Required technical anchors: check lossless-priority configuration, PFC/ECN, MTU, route symmetry, congestion, NIC counters, queue pairs, and whether a fallback path is hiding the real fault. It must report topology, workload, units, baselines, confounders, and evidence needed before claiming improvement.
corrected_answer:
Assume a multi-node GPU collective using RoCE, but verify the NIC, switch, VLAN/priority mapping, MTU, routing, congestion-control policy, collective library, topology, and software versions. Treat the path as a hypothesis: the library posts verbs work requests to queue pairs backed by registered buffers; Ethernet frames traverse the selected routes, and completion behavior, retransmission, PFC/ECN response, timeout handling, or an alternate path determine application-visible latency. RoCE is not automatically lossless or low-tail; queue buildup, pause propagation, route asymmetry, MTU mismatch, incast, oversubscription, PCIe placement, and fallback can dominate.

Hypothesis: under fixed model, message sizes, node count, topology, routes, MTU, traffic mix, software, clocks, and background load, correcting the suspected RoCE control-plane/data-plane condition reduces p95/p99 collective latency (ms) and timeout rate while preserving throughput (GB/s and samples/s or tokens/s). Establish a known-good baseline and capture per-operation application latency, p50/p95/p99/max, bytes, achieved bandwidth, queue depth and completions, retries/timeouts, ECN marks, PFC pause frames, drops, NIC link errors, retransmits, route/path identity, GPU utilization, host CPU, and end-to-end step latency. Check lossless-priority classification in both directions, PFC scope, ECN marking/feedback, MTU consistency, route symmetry, queue-pair placement, congestion hotspots, and whether a fallback path is carrying traffic. Use matched workload replay, warm-up exclusion, repeated randomized trials, synchronized timestamps, and report units, topology, baselines, sample counts, confounders, and raw evidence.

For a link failure or timeout storm, stop or drain the affected traffic, preserve counters and logs, bound retries, and do not increase timeouts until congestion and correctness are understood. Quarantine the suspect route or port and switch to a tested alternate path/transport only after validating capacity, ordering, and collective correctness; otherwise pause the job. Roll back the change if p99/max latency, timeout/error rate, correctness, or throughput violates the predeclared gate, then restore the known-good configuration and canary gradually. Evidence required: switch/NIC configuration, route and priority maps, packet/counter traces, controlled fault injection, matched baseline/A-B results, and proof that no fallback hid the RoCE fault. Do not invent vendor-specific settings or disclose credentials.
